title: Concurrent Add site imports in one dsh process keep every site's line in the JSON books and never fail on a shared temp file
steps: S1: Run packages/site/tracy-add-site/test/book-race.test.mjs: three sites write upload cursors 40 times each at once (rememberUpload), one site is forgotten while the others write (forgetUpload), and the same for site-tokens.json (rememberToken/forgetToken) and handovers.json (rememberPartial/rememberHandover/forgetHandover); the same import result is queued 20 times at once (reportImportResult). Also: a sweep (takeOrSweep) paused inside remove while a new run writes its own dump for the same site.
S2: Run the cold-cache concurrent read test in packages/design/tracy-design-inspiration/test/library-remote.test.mjs: 20 reads of one system file at once before it is cached.
S3: Run the two-undos test in apps/tracy-host/test/ds-slot.test.mjs: two undo jobs of one design-system entry at once.
expect: S1: no call throws; each book holds exactly the sites still remembered; no *.tmp file is left; no 'could not queue import operation result' warning. The same-site sweep removes only the old dump and the new line survives.
S2: every reader gets the file's bytes; no *.tmp file is left.
S3: one undo answers ok, the other {ok:false, code:'DS_UNDO_USED'}; the manifest is marked reverted; no *.tmp file is left.
evidence: Production dsh log 20/10/2026: a Joomla import failed at reading_files with ENOENT rename uploads.json.1.tmp -> uploads.json while a WordPress import was uploading parts; uploads.json then held only the other site's entry
fence: Per-write unique temp names and a per-file serialised read-modify-write in the plugin's book helper; per-entry serialised undo in the ds-slot job

tests: upload cursors of several sites written at once all survive
forgetting one site while others write keeps the others
site tokens written and forgotten at once keep every remembered site
handover lines of several sites written at once all survive
the same import result queued twice at once does not lose its temp file
the same system file read many times at once, before it is cached, answers every reader
two undos of one entry at once: one puts it back, the other is refused, neither throws
a new line written for the same site while the sweep deletes the old dump is kept
